title: Every line is oozing
objective: Recognize DIC from its laboratory pattern -- prolonged clotting times, low fibrinogen, falling platelets -- treat the trigger, and give blood components for bleeding
secondaryObjectives: Coagulopathies such as ITP, DIC and HIT, and managing bleeding and clotting disorders

brief.situation: 16:00 in a medical ICU. You are Mrs. Delgado's nurse. She is 58, admitted at 04:00 in septic shock from a urinary source, on the ordered norepinephrine and antibiotics. The aide says her gums are bleeding.
handover: Lines: a right internal jugular central line and a radial arterial line, both placed this morning.
A CT this morning showed an obstructing ureteral stone with hydronephrosis; the radiology report posted at noon. Urology has not been called.

Scheduled: the ordered enoxaparin for VTE prophylaxis at 17:00. Unit policy: blood components only on the intensivist's order; bleeding precautions (no IM injections, pressure at sites, soft toothbrush) for any patient who is bleeding.
howItWorks: The clock runs in simulated time; study pace runs three simulated minutes per real minute. Pause any time.
Each assessment takes the time on its button. Decide what the findings mean, what to stop or start, and who must know.
Partway through you are asked to write your reasoning. A debrief scores what you did.

then.log: Platelets 38 (162 at 04:00); INR 2.4 and aPTT 61 s, both up; fibrinogen low at 90 mg/dL; D-dimer markedly high; schistocytes on the smear. Hemoglobin 8.1 from 10.4.
Blood oozing through both line dressings; gums bleeding; urine pink; petechiae on her arms; pupils equal, she follows commands.
The CT shows an obstructing ureteral stone with hydronephrosis: an undrained infected kidney. Antibiotics running; no drainage arranged.
Enoxaparin for VTE prophylaxis due at 17:00; no other anticoagulant or antiplatelet.

why.question: What is happening to her clotting, why, and what do you do?

parts.label: What and why
parts.criteria: Overt DIC: falling platelets, prolonged PT/INR and aPTT, low fibrinogen, high D-dimer and schistocytes, with bleeding; triggered by sepsis from an undrained obstructed kidney.
parts.modelAnswer: This is DIC. Her platelets fell from 162 to 38, her INR and aPTT are up, her fibrinogen is low and her D-dimer is high, and she's bleeding from every site. Sepsis from the blocked, infected kidney is driving it.

parts.label: What I do
parts.criteria: Treats the trigger (source control of the obstructed kidney, antibiotics continue); components for active bleeding (platelets, plasma, cryoprecipitate) on order; holds the prophylactic anticoagulant while bleeding; bleeding precautions; calls now, not after a repeat panel.
parts.modelAnswer: Call the intensivist now: she needs the kidney drained, because the trigger has to be treated, and platelets, plasma and cryo for the bleeding. Hold the enoxaparin, put pressure on the sites and start bleeding precautions.

noProgress.rationale: Bleeding DIC left without components or source control for an hour is harm here.

hemorrhage.headline: Hemorrhagic shock
hemorrhage.body: Falling platelets, long clotting times, low fibrinogen and a high D-dimer with bleeding is DIC. Treat the trigger, give components for the bleeding and hold anticoagulants.

controlled.headline: Recognized and treated
controlled.body: You recognized overt DIC from the lab pattern, held the enoxaparin, called within minutes for components and source control, and protected the bleeding sites. That is the expert path.

controlledGaps.headline: To drainage, with gaps
controlledGaps.body: Check how soon you called, whether the components ran, and whether the enoxaparin went in.

time_up.headline: No plan
time_up.body: Bleeding DIC needs the trigger treated and components given within the hour.

scoring.modelReasoning: Platelets falling from 162 to 38, a prolonged INR and aPTT, low fibrinogen, a high D-dimer and schistocytes with bleeding from every site is overt DIC. Sepsis from an undrained obstructed kidney is the trigger, so treatment starts there: antibiotics continue and the kidney is drained urgently. Because she is actively bleeding, she gets platelets, plasma and cryoprecipitate on order, the prophylactic enoxaparin is held, and bleeding precautions protect the sites. The call goes now, not after a repeat panel.
